notes: Every recorded body here was copied from an existing InferHub.Client dotnet test literal, itself captured from a real hub or, where the test file says so, derived from the hub's own serializer/source. Nothing in this file was hand-typed from a schema. See conformance/README.md for the case schema and dotnet/tests/InferHub.Client.Tests/ConformanceCorpusTests.cs for the runner.

cases.description: A solo node's /api/status.retrieval.rerank is the config-level rerank MODE ("none"|"llm"), never a boolean. dotnet/v1.7.0 typed it bool? and threw a JsonException the first time it was driven against a real node with retrieval on; fixed in v1.7.1. This is the corpus's founding case: found by installing the published package and driving a real hub, not by reading the client.
The hub's /api/status carries no `mode` field at all, ever - that absence, not a value, is half of ProbeAsync's discriminator.
NDJSON inference ends with {"error":...,"done":true} rather than a transport failure. A client that only checks `done` hangs; one that only checks HTTP status reports success.
Retrieval asked for and unavailable is HTTP 424, a different condition from a missing model (404), and needs its own exception type.
X-InferHub-Sources arrives as a JSON array most of the time.

A real hub has also sent X-InferHub-Sources comma-separated rather than as a JSON array. A client that only tries JSON.parse loses the ids on this shape - spec/README.md calls this the corpus's first case.

/api/* answers {"error":"..."}; /v1/* answers {"error":{"message":...,"type":...,"param":...,"code":...}} - an OpenAI SDK reads error.message. Which envelope arrived decides the exception type, never which method was called.

response.body: {"error":{"message":"no provider 'openrouter' serves model 'gemma:2b' on this hub. The X-InferHub-Provider header can only choose among the providers already configured for a model; 'node' keeps the request on the fleet.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"model","code":null}}

cases.description: The refused-steer 400 carries param but code:null. A client that treats a missing code as "not an OpenAI envelope" loses the message.

response.body: {"error":{"message":"response_format=url is not supported: this coordinator never stores a generated image, so there is no URL to serve it from. Use response_format=b64_json.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"response_format","code":null}}

cases.description: "the fleet holds this model but nobody is doing this kind of work right now" is 503 + Retry-After and worth retrying; a missing model is 404 with nothing to wait for. Not the same condition.

A streamed /v1 frame with an empty choices array is the usage frame - the only place a streamed call reports token counts. A client that skips frames with no choices reports "usage: not available" for every stream.

The hub answers a partial ingest with an error status on purpose, but the body is complete and the chunks that landed are real. A client that maps every 5xx onto an exception throws away the document id.

Reranking sorts by what a chat model said and leaves every score untouched, so a reranked hit list routinely starts with a LOWER score than the hit below it. A client that sorts by score to be tidy silently undoes the rerank its caller paid for.

cases.description: The chunks route hands the chunk index back as a string (chunk metadata is a string map on the hub); a search hit's `page` is a real int on the same corpus. A client that types `index` as an int fails to deserialize.
